page.layout: One column of italic verse, full width, five stanzas of four lines each; below the last stanza, at the right, one catchword "SATYRÆ"; a printed ornament (tailpiece) below that, not transcribed. Page number and running head at the top.

p.i: Chordis sonoris hinc tua barbitos, / Pralustris Orphei pectine clarior, / Gratesmobilitas auebit / Pro meritis cecinisse Christo.
Lucerna vestræ fulgida lampadis, / Callens, micantum de face crinium / Illius, accendisse flamam / Sideribus radiantiorem,
Caecutientes, Cimmerium genus, / Asepticollis[?] tramite verticis / Dimouit, errorisque monstrat / Califeros humeros Atlantis.
O vivat, o lucem alterius Poli / Illustriorem porrigat in solum / Tenebricosa sorde mersum, / Beza, meum decus & Lemanni!
O Galliarum sidus Olympium, / Umbras avita Tartareas humo / Defende, collabentis ulvo[?] / Viderimus Babylonis arces.

page.notes: Line breaks within each stanza are marked by " / ". Doubtful readings: "Pralustris" and "Gratesmobilitas" (letters blurred), "Asepticollis" (the word after "Asepticollis" is also partly blurred), "ulvo" (printed form unclear). Long s has been written as plain s throughout. Spelling u/v adjusted as per convention ("auebit" to "avebit", "viuat" to "vivat", "Vmbras" to "Umbras"); the text otherwise follows the printed letters. Printed ornament at the foot of the page omitted. Line-end mark after "humo" is a printed dash-like stroke, not transcribed.
